questions.stem: Which blood vessel brings nutrient-rich blood from the intestines directly to the liver?
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood directly from the intestines to the liver. This allows the liver to process absorbed nutrients and remove any toxins before the blood reaches the rest of the body.

questions.stem: What is the process of converting toxic ammonia to less toxic urea called?
questions.explanation: The ornithine cycle (also called the urea cycle) converts toxic ammonia into less toxic urea in the liver. Deamination is the earlier step where the amino group is removed from amino acids to produce ammonia.

questions.stem: Why can the body NOT store excess amino acids?

options.text: The nitrogen-containing amino group would become toxic
The liver does not have receptors for amino acids
Amino acids are too large to fit inside cells
Amino acids dissolve in water too easily

questions.explanation: The body cannot store excess amino acids because the nitrogen-containing amino group cannot be stored safely. If excess amino acids accumulated, the ammonia produced would be toxic, so deamination must occur to safely remove the nitrogen.

questions.stem: What is the role of detoxification in the liver?

options.text: To produce bile for fat digestion
To break down harmful substances like alcohol into less toxic forms

questions.explanation: Detoxification is the process by which the liver converts harmful substances (such as alcohol, drugs, and hormones) into less toxic or harmless forms. For example, alcohol is broken down by the enzyme alcohol dehydrogenase.

questions.stem: What happens to the keto acid produced during deamination?

options.text: It is used in respiration or converted to fat

questions.explanation: When an amino acid is deaminated, it produces ammonia and a keto acid. The keto acid (the remaining carbon-based part) is not wasted; it can be used in aerobic respiration to release energy or converted to fat for storage.

questions.stem: A common misconception is that the liver excretes urea. What actually happens?

options.text: Urea is made in the blood and excreted by the skin
The kidneys make urea, and the liver excretes it
The liver both makes and excretes urea
The liver makes urea, but the kidneys excrete it

questions.explanation: The liver produces urea from ammonia (via the ornithine cycle), but it does not excrete it. Urea is released into the blood and transported to the kidneys, which filter it out and excrete it in urine.

questions.stem: Which condition results from long-term alcohol damage to the liver?
questions.explanation: Cirrhosis is the scarring of liver tissue caused by long-term damage, most commonly from excessive alcohol consumption or hepatitis infection. The scarring reduces liver function and can eventually lead to liver failure.
